detail.name: National Identity Management Commission
detail.summary: For NIN Pre-enrolment and NIN Verification
detail.about: The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) established by the NIMC Act No. 23 of 2007, has the mandate to establish, own, operate, maintain and manage the National Identity Database in Nigeria, register persons covered by the Act, assign a Unique National Identification Number (NIN) and issue General Multi-Purpose Cards (GMPC) to those who are citizens of Nigeria as well as others legally residing within the country. The NIMC Act 2007 provides for the establishment of the NIMC, its functions, powers, establishment of the National Identity Database, assignment of the National Identification Number (NIN) as well as issuance of token General Multi-purpose cards. The Act also provides the Commission with powers to make regulations connected with its functions. The NIMC Act 2007 provides the repeal of the law that created the former Department of National Civic Registration (DNCR) and the transfer of its assets and liabilities to the NIMC.

Step 5: Applicant has his/her supporting documents scanned.

services.name: SMEDAN (SMEDAN One-Stop Portal)
services.summary: SMEDAN One-Stop Portal is a flagship initiative overseen by SMEDAN / Ministry of Industry, Trade & Investment. Its primary purpose is provide support and resources to SMEs through financial, technical and capacity-building interventions The programme operates through a clearly defined application process which is hosted on the official portal (https://smedan.gov.ng), and includes online registration, verification and monitoring elements. Applicants are usually required to provide digital documentation, meet eligibility criteria set by the administering agency, and comply with reporting and repayment guidelines where applicable. The programme's design emphasises transparency, measurable outcomes and linkage to other support services such as training, market access and technical assistance. Beneficiaries typically gain access to financial or technical inputs, and the scheme includes monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to measure impact and ensure funds reach intended recipients. The initiative is often complemented by partner institutions and private sector actors to scale impact.

detail.name: Bureau of Public Procurement
detail.about: The Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) is a federal government agency in Nigeria established under the Public Procurement Act of 2007. It serves as the primary regulatory body for public procurement, ensuring transparency, accountability, and efficiency in the acquisition of goods, works, and services by Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs). The BPP operates under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Finance and collaborates with the National Council on Public Procurement (NCPP) to set policies and standards. Its role includes monitoring procurement processes, issuing Certificates of No-Objection, maintaining a national database of contractors, and promoting capacity building for procurement professionals.
detail.vision: To establish a transparent, efficient, and competitive public procurement system in Nigeria that aligns with global best practices and delivers optimal value for public resources.

detail.name: Federal Road Safety Corps
detail.about:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) is a Nigerian federal government agency established in February 1988 under Decree No. 45 of 1988, amended by Decree 35 of 1992, and codified as the FRSC Act Cap 141, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria. The FRSC (Establishment) Act 2007 further formalized its role as Nigeria’s lead agency for road safety administration and traffic management. Headquartered at No. 4 Maputo Street, Zone 3, Wuse, Abuja, the FRSC operates across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing. Its mandate includes:

  • Preventing and minimizing road traffic crashes on highways.
  • Clearing road obstructions to ensure smooth traffic flow.
  • Educating drivers and the public on road safety and proper highway use.
  • Issuing driver’s licenses and vehicle number plates.
  • Enforcing standardized highway traffic codes and speed limits.
  • Providing prompt rescue services and medical care to accident victims.
  • Conducting research on accident causes and implementing preventive measures.
  • Regulating safety devices (e.g., seat belts, helmets) and mobile phone use by motorists.
  • Collaborating with stakeholders to enhance road safety.
  • Enforcing traffic laws with powers to arrest and prosecute offenders.
detail.vision: To eradicate road traffic crashes and create a safe motoring environment in Nigeria, working towards achieving zero road traffic deaths through 100% dedication to safety initiatives and global best practices.
detail.mission:
The mission of the FRSC is to regulate, enforce, and coordinate all road traffic and safety management activities through:

  • Sustained public enlightenment campaigns to educate road users on traffic rules and safety measures.
  • Effective patrol operations to enforce compliance with traffic regulations.
  • Prompt rescue services to provide immediate assistance to accident victims.
  • Improved vehicle administration, including registration and roadworthiness checks.
  • Robust data management to inform policy and accident prevention strategies.
  • Promotion of stakeholder cooperation with government agencies, private organizations, and international partners to enhance road safety initiatives.

detail.name: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation, and Digital Economy
detail.about: The Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE) is a key government institution in Nigeria, established in 2011 (formerly as the Federal Ministry of Communications Technology). It serves as the primary provider for policies and initiatives driving Nigeria's digital transformation. The ministry's mandate is to accelerate the diversification of the Nigerian economy by enhancing productivity in critical sectors through digital technology and innovation. This includes fostering a knowledge-based economy, promoting information and communication technology (ICT) for job creation, economic growth, and transparent governance. FMCIDE oversees 12 departments, 5 units, and 7 agencies, focusing on areas like infrastructure development, policy implementation, and stakeholder collaboration to build a robust digital ecosystem.

detail.name: Nigerian Postal Service

NIPOST holds the exclusive mandate as the designated Universal Service Provider (USP) for postal services in Nigeria, fulfilling the Universal Service Obligation (USO) as per the Nigerian Postal Services Act of 1992. This includes maintaining a nationwide network for affordable, reliable public services, particularly in underserved rural areas. Its core responsibilities encompass:

  • Postal and Allied Services: Providing collection, dispatch, distribution, and delivery of mail, parcels, and documents domestically and internationally to individuals and corporate bodies.
  • Financial and Counter Services: Operating money orders, savings accounts, pension payments, and e-government services (e.g., vehicle license renewals, exam form sales).
  • Regulatory Role: Overseeing courier and logistics operators through licensing, monitoring, and enforcement to ensure sector standards.
  • International Representation: Representing Nigeria in global bodies like the Universal Postal Union (UPU), Pan African Postal Union (PAPU), and West African Postal Conference (WAPCO).
  • Innovation and Expansion: Facilitating e-commerce logistics, philatelic services (stamps and memorabilia), and non-postal ventures like microfinance and property management to promote socio-economic development.

NIPOST's mandate emphasizes bridging geographical gaps, supporting SMEs, and integrating with digital economy initiatives, such as verifiable digital addressing in partnership with the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC).

detail.name: Nigeria Immigration Service
detail.about:
The NIS serves as the primary provider of immigration and border management services in Nigeria. Its mandate, as outlined in the Immigration Act 2015 and subsequent regulations, focuses on securing national borders while promoting economic prosperity through efficient migration policies. Key responsibilities include:

  • Aliens Control and Border Patrol Management: Monitoring and regulating the entry, stay, and exit of non-Nigerians (aliens) to prevent illegal immigration, human trafficking, and smuggling. This involves patrolling land, sea, and air borders, with recent enhancements like the inauguration of over 100 trained personnel for surveillance infrastructure in October 2024.
  • Issuance of Travel Documents: Since 1988, the NIS has been responsible for all Nigerian passports, visas, residence permits (e.g., CERPAC for expatriates), and other travel documents. This includes online applications, biometric enrollment, and innovations like contactless passport renewals via mobile app for eligible applicants.
  • Migration Management and Security: Enforcing immigration laws, deporting violators, and maintaining a national database for population and border control. The service also handles e-Visa systems, Landing and Exit Cards, and migrant registration for those staying over 90 days.
  • Additional Duties: Facilitating ECOWAS free movement protocols, combating transnational crime, and supporting citizen diplomacy through passport interventions abroad. The NIS operates under the Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board (CDCFIB), which oversees paramilitary services to ensure peace, safety, and stability.

detail.mission: To strengthen the security and prosperity of Nigeria through proactive, effective, and efficient border security and migration management.

detail.name: National Youth Service Corps
detail.about:
The core mandate of NYSC, as outlined in the National Youth Service Corps Act of 1993, is to mobilize Nigerian graduate youths for national service, emphasizing national integration, labor mobility, and youth development. It aims to provide service in areas like national unity, sustainable development, and self-reliance while preparing participants for leadership challenges. The four cardinal objectives are:

  • To inculcate discipline in Nigerian youths through industry, patriotism, and loyal service.
  • To develop common ties among youths and promote national unity and integration.
  • To raise the moral tone of youths by exposing them to ideals of national achievement, social, and cultural improvement.
  • To remove prejudices, eliminate ignorance, and highlight similarities among Nigerians of all ethnic groups.

These objectives are pursued through a structured service year, including orientation camps, primary assignments (often in rural areas focusing on education, health, agriculture, and infrastructure), community development service (CDS), and national integration activities.
detail.vision: NYSC envisions being at the forefront of national development efforts, serving as a platform to impart values of nationalism, patriotism, loyalty, and accountable leadership in youths. detail.name: Nigerian Export Promotion Council

NEPC was created to address the need for a coordinated approach to export promotion in Nigeria, particularly to boost non-oil sectors amid economic diversification efforts. The enabling Decree No. 26 of 1976 empowered it as the primary federal agency for export development. Its core mandate encompasses:

  • Coordinating and harmonizing export development and promotion activities across the country.
  • Leading national export programs, including policy implementation and incentive distribution.
  • Interfacing with international trade agencies for cooperation, capacity building, and market access.
  • Promoting the development and diversification of Nigeria's export trade, with a focus on non-oil products such as agricultural commodities, semi-processed goods, solid minerals, and manufactured items.
  • Advising the government on export policies, providing technical support to exporters (e.g., documentation, standardization, and packaging), and maintaining a database of verified Nigerian exporters for global buyers.

NEPC's operations support broader goals like the Zero Oil Plan and initiatives such as the Export Expansion Facility Programme (EEFP) and "Operation Double Your Export," aimed at increasing non-oil export volumes to $5 billion annually by enhancing competitiveness and reducing reliance on crude oil revenues.

detail.name: Nigerian Communications Commission
detail.about:
The NCC was established under the Nigerian Communications Act (NCA) 2003, signed into law on July 8, 2003, to create a regulatory framework for the Nigerian communications industry. Its primary mandate includes:

  • Developing and enforcing licensing, regulatory frameworks, and performance standards for telecommunications services to ensure quality, affordability, and universal access.
  • Managing the national frequency spectrum, numbering plan, and electronic addresses in collaboration with the National Frequency Management Council.
  • Promoting fair competition, encouraging local and foreign investments, and fostering innovation in the sector.
  • Implementing universal service provision programs and monitoring industry performance to support Nigeria's economic growth.

The NCC operates as an independent regulatory body under the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, focusing on a market-driven industry.

detail.name: National Information Technology Development Agency
detail.about:
National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) was created in April 2001 to implement the Nigerian Information Technology Policy and co-ordinate general IT development in the country.

Our Act (National Information Technology Development Act (2007) mandate us to create a framework for the planning, research, development, standardization, application, coordination, monitoring, evaluation and regulation of Information Technology practices, activities and systems in Nigeria.

Our role therefore is to develop, regulate and advise on Information technology in the country through regulatory standards, guidelines and policies. Additionally, NITDA is the clearing house for all IT projects and infrastructural development in the country. It is the prime Agency for e-government implementation, Internet governance and general IT development in Nigeria.

NITDA is poised to actualise its mammoth mandate through strategic and inclusive stakeholder management, local and international partnership and efficient utilisation of resources in the interest of Nigeria

detail.name: Federal Ministry of Science, Technology & Innovation
Galaxy Backbone
detail.about:
Galaxy Backbone (GBB) is the information technology and shared services provider of the Federal Government of Nigeria, established in 2006 to eliminate the technology silos that had developed across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), and to build a common services platform — including in-country and offshore VSAT hubs, a data centre, a Federal Capital metro fibre backbone, and multiple redundant internet gateways. As mandated by its supervising ministry (currently FMCIDE — please confirm current supervisory arrangement), Galaxy Backbone is responsible for:


Being the provider of shared ICT infrastructure, applications, and services to all Federal Government MDAs and institutions.

Building and operating a single nationwide IP broadband network to deliver network services to all Federal Government MDAs and institutions.

Deploying and maintaining national database management systems and transversal government applications, including government-wide messaging and collaboration tools, the federal public service personnel and payroll system, and the government gateway and national portal.

Setting standards and guidelines for MDAs' acquisition and acceptable use of ICT infrastructure, applications, and services.

Providing Wide Area Networks (WAN) and Metropolitan Area Networks (MAN) connecting government entities.

Providing technical support to the supervising ministry for end-to-end quality assurance of ICT projects and capacity building for government ICT professionals.
